name: What happens to the wall and backsplash when an old bathroom countertop is removed?

mainEntity.name: What happens to the wall and backsplash when an old bathroom countertop is removed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a bathroom countertop often disturbs the adjacent drywall, paint, or existing wall tile, especially when pulling off an old glued backsplash. As a hands-on general and finish contractor, Abraham Becerra directly handles interior drywall repair, texture matching, and painting, as well as custom tile installation. If the old top pulled off drywall paper or left an uneven gap, our crew patches the wall surface, installs a fresh tile backsplash if desired, and blends paint seamlessly, ensuring you do not have to hire separate dry-wallers or painters to complete the room.
acceptedAnswer.description: Removing glued tops often damages adjacent drywall. Our crew repairs the drywall, repaints, or installs custom tile backsplashes directly as part of the overall finish work.
